articles.title: Swept away by raging Teesta in Bengal, elephant calf saved by four fishermen
articles.summary: Jalpaiguri fishermen rescued a newborn elephant calf from the Teesta, aided forest teams, and helped reunite it with its mother after two hours.
articles.body: Jalpaiguri: Five Jalpaiguri fishermen on a small row boat pulled off a miraculous rescue on Teesta as they pulled up a newborn elephant calf on Monday. The calf had been swept away nearly 4 km downstream while its herd was crossing the river near Apalchand forest’s Kathambari range.Spotting the calf struggling to stay afloat, Bablu Das, Mithun Das, Kader Das, Biswanath and Gopal braved the swollen river’s strong currents and rowed their boat to the elephant. The calf was gasping for breath, with its little trunk raised above the water as the waves continued to push it further downstream. Three of the fishermen jumped off and the calf was hauled on to the boat. As the boat returned, the three swam alongside the boat, pushing it against the current.The calf was handed over to forest personnel upon reaching the bank. It was taken to the Kathambari range office and given immediate veterinary care.Earlier on Monday, a herd of five elephants was moving upstream of Gajoldoba Teesta Barrage when currents separated the calf. The fishermen spotted it floating near the 12th spur of Teesta, close to Punjab embankment.Following the rescue, teams from Baikunthapur forest division began efforts to locate the mother. The calf was transported across the barrage to a dry stretch of Teesta riverbed, where the herd was believed to have taken shelter.After nearly two hours of coordinated efforts of foresters, locals and fishermen, the calf was successfully reunited with its mother. The mother elephant approached the calf and was later seen nursing it.Baikunthapur DFO Mudit lauded the fishermen for their timely action, saying it was crucial for the reunion. Elephants often don’t take back calves into the herd if they are exposed to humans for long. articles.title: Naga teen on way to buy essentials killed in Manipur ambush
articles.summary: 17-year-old Naga boy NK Wiphenbou was killed in an alleged ambush by suspected Kuki militants in Manipur’s Tamenglong while going to buy essentials, police said.
articles.body: GUWAHATI: A 17-year-old boy from the Naga community was killed in an alleged ambush by suspected Kuki militants in Manipur’s Tamenglong district on Monday morning, police said, as tensions between the two communities escalated.The victim, identified as NK Wiphenbou, was reportedly travelling alone from Upper Takou village to Tamei town to buy essential commodities when he came under attack at around 10.30am. Naga village volunteers later reportedly found his body along a narrow pathway.“Based on the spot examination, he is suspected to have been ambushed. From the public enquiries and statements gathered so far, suspected Kuki militants carried out the ambush,” a senior police officer told TOI, ruling out the possibility that the boy had been caught in crossfire.Different versions have emerged about the circumstances leading to his death. However, according to police sources, there was no exchange of fire when the boy was killed.Awangbow Newmai, MLA from Tamei assembly constituency, said Wiphenbou, a resident of Upper Takou village under Tamei subdivision in Tamenglong district, was ambushed and killed.In a social media post, Newmai alleged that the ambush was carried out by Kuki militants between Upper Takou and Tamah (Malek) while the boy was travelling towards Tamei to buy essential commodities for his family.“I unequivocally condemn the cowardly and heinous acts of terrorism that target innocent civilians and threaten peace and security. Such barbaric violence has no justification and no place in a civilised society,” Newmai wrote in a note of condemnation.Former Manipur CM N Biren Singh urged the authorities to act decisively, establish accountability and bring those responsible to justice without delay.“Today, it is 17-year-old NK Wiphenbou. Who will be next?” Biren wrote in a social media post.“The killing of this young student from Upper Takou village, while he was travelling to buy essential commodities, is deeply painful. Manipur cannot continue to lose innocent lives to this endless cycle of violence,” he said.The latest incident marks a widening of the conflict beyond the Kuki-Meitei confrontation that has dominated Manipur since ethnic clashes erupted in May 2023. Over the past 10 days, five Kuki villagers have been killed in separate incidents allegedly involving suspected Naga militants, fuelling fresh tensions across the state’s hill districts.Several houses have also been torched in Naga and Kuki-inhabited areas, with Kangpokpi, Tamenglong and Noney among the worst-hit districts.Meanwhile, a 24-hour bandh called in Manipur on Monday to oppose the 1949 Manipur Merger Agreement received a mixed response across the state. The bandh, called by the proscribed outfit National Revolutionary Front Manipur (NRFM) from midnight on Sunday, disrupted normal life in the Valley districts.Markets, businesses and educational institutions remained closed in parts of the Valley. Imphal saw thin vehicular movement amid heavy deployment of police and security forces. Inter-state transport services were also disrupted, while emergency and healthcare services were exempted.Two days earlier, an active NRFM cadre, Namoijam Boboi Mangang, 39, was arrested at Gate 1 of Regional Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS), Lamphel, under Lamphel police station in Imphal West district.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.summary: Dipke alleges CM Fadnavis is shielding MPSC chief Vivek Bhimanwar amid exam irregularity claims; BJP dismisses it as “Mungerilal ke Sapne.”
articles.body: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday accused chief minister Devendra Fadnavis of shielding Maharashtra Public Service Commission chairperson Vivek Bhimanwar amid growing allegations of irregularities. BJP dismissed Dipke’s claims as baseless “daydreaming” driven by political motives.“Was he made MPSC chairperson because he was your senior in college? Personal equations should remain private,” he said, targeting Fadnavis at a gathering of MPSC candidates in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, which organisers said was attended by around 2,000 aspirants.BJP spokesperson Sanjay Kenekar dismissed Dipke’s claims as “nothing but Mungerilal Ke Haseen Sapne,” accusing him of acting as an Aam Aadmi Party “agent.” “Fadnavis leads a govt that secured a clear electoral mandate,” he said.Dipke said confidence in MPSC had eroded and insisted that Bhimanwar’s removal was necessary to restore trust. “Aspirants have lost faith in MPSC. If question papers are being leaked repeatedly, students have no reason to trust the system. To rebuild confidence, the chairperson must be removed,” Dipke said.He said protests would continue till Bhimanwar resigned, questioning why he remained in office despite allegations raised by aspirants over the conduct of recruitment examinations. Highlighting the scale of the aspirants’ community, Dipke said nearly 20 lakh MPSC candidates and their families constituted a significant voter base. “If Bhimanwar is not made to resign, aspirants will not support you. Leave aside him, you could lose your own post,” he warned.In a statement issued later, CJP said Dipke had urged students to join the “Bhimanwar Should Resign” campaign by posting videos on social media outlining their concerns and demanding accountability from MPSC leadership.According to the party, the meeting focused on alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations and the need for accountability within the commission. Dipke had held a similar interaction with aspirants in Amravati on Sept 19, while another outreach meeting is planned in Nashik.The CJP statement also cited a March 2025 Loksatta report that raised questions over the procurement of radar equipment for interceptor vehicles during Bhimanwar’s tenure as Maharashtra transport commissioner. articles.title: Grounds in writing a must during arrests even in UAPA: Supreme Court
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Holding that fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution cannot be interpreted in a restrictive manner, Supreme Court on Monday he.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Holding that fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution cannot be interpreted in a restrictive manner, Supreme Court on Monday held that a person's personal liberty cannot be invaded except in accordance with the procedure established by the Constitution, even if accused of a grave offence and anti-social activities, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.Elucidating Article 22 of the Constitution, which offers protection against arrest and detention in certain cases, a bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar said a person must be provided with the grounds of arrest by the probe agency at the time of arrest in writing and its language understandable to the accused. SC said this is applicable in all cases including under special laws - such as PMLA and UAPA - regardless of the nature and gravity of offence.'Court nod required for re-arrest when flouting Article 22'Going a step further, the bench said that if a person's arrest is declared illegal for non-compliance with Article 22, then he or she cannot be re-arrested in the same case without approval from a senior police officer and nod from the court concerned."We need to remind ourselves that Constitution or a constitutional provision cannot be interpreted in a vacuum. Interpretation of Constitution cannot also be left to imponderables in the form of ifs and buts. Constitution is based on certain basic principles, much above the statutory threshold. Therefore, violation of Constitution or a constitutional provision cannot be countenanced. It has to be dealt with strictly. It is not dependent on the nature or gravity of the offence, encompassing within its sweep all offences. It cannot be interpreted in a restrictive manner," the bench said. Referring to SC's verdict in the Prabhu Dayal Deorah case on preventive detention, the court said, "The gravity of the evil to the community resulting from anti-social activities can never furnish an adequate reason for invading the personal liberty of a citizen, except in accordance with the procedure established by Constitution and laws."The bench said that when a person is arrested, his right to liberty under Article 21 is curtailed and it is necessary that the person must understand on what grounds he has been arrested."The requirement of informing the arrested person the grounds of arrest in the light of and under Article 22(1) is not a mere formality but a mandatory binding constitutional safeguard. Thus, if a person is not informed of the grounds of his arrest as soon as may be, it would amount to violation of his fundamental rights thereby curtailing his right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 of Constitution, rendering the arrest illegal," the bench said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Charles Barkley pledged $1 million to a New Orleans high school after two students made a historic maths discovery
articles.summary: US News: St. Mary’s Academy in New Orleans received a $1 million pledge from former NBA star Charles Barkley after two of its students made a unique breakthrou.
articles.body: St. Mary’s Academy in New Orleans received a $1 million pledge from former NBA star Charles Barkley after two of its students made a unique breakthrough in mathematics. Calcea Johnson and Ne’Kiya Jackson, then high-school seniors, developed a new proof of the 2,000-year-old Pythagorean theorem using trigonometry. Their work attracted attention after they presented it to the American Mathematical Society, and Barkley later saw their achievement on television. The story prompted him to support the school and the opportunities it gives students beyond the classroom.How Charles Barkley pledged $1 million after a historic maths discoveryJohnson and Jackson were students at St. Mary’s Academy when they began working on a problem that had challenged mathematicians for generations. The Pythagorean theorem describes the relationship between the three sides of a right-angled triangle and has been known since ancient times.What made the students’ work unique was the method they used. According to BasketballNetwork, they proved the theorem through trigonometry, despite a long-standing belief that such an approach could lead to circular reasoning because many familiar trigonometric formulas are connected to the theorem itself.The pair found a way around that problem by using the Law of Sines. Their approach showed that the trigonometric relationship they relied on did not necessarily depend on the Pythagorean theorem, allowing them to construct their proof without assuming the result they were trying to establish. Barkley became aware of the students through coverage of their achievement. After watching them on TV, he decided to pledge $1 million to St. Mary’s Academy.The former NBA star has spoken publicly about encouraging young Black students to consider careers beyond sports and entertainment. BasketballNetwork reported that Barkley has often urged students to think about professions such as medicine, law, engineering and teaching rather than seeing athletics as their only path. Their work gave him an example of the kind of academic accomplishment he had been encouraging students to pursue.Why the students’ mathematical proof was so challengingThe discovery was not the result of a quick classroom exercise. The SportsRush reported that Johnson and Jackson worked on the problem for months, with Johnson’s parents recalling how many pages of calculations accumulated during the process.Their work was eventually submitted for recognition at an American Mathematical Society conference in March 2023. By then, teachers and their families understood that the students had produced something far beyond an ordinary school assignment.St. Mary’s Academy will use the $1 million pledge to support studentsThe donation was structured as a 10-year gift rather than a single payment. Axios reported that the first part of Barkley’s $1 million donation had arrived at St. Mary’s Academy by September 2024.The school said the money would be used to strengthen its educational experience and create more opportunities for students to develop both inside the classroom and within the New Orleans community. St. Mary’s president Pamela Rogers described the gift as support for students as they pursue the ambitions they develop during their time at the school, as reported by Axios.Where these 2 students continued their studiesJohnson and Jackson had already moved on from St. Mary’s by the time Barkley’s donation was announced. Axios reported that Johnson became a student at Louisiana State University, while Jackson began studying at Xavier University.Their paths after high school also show how quickly an extraordinary school achievement can become part of a longer academic journey. For the school, their work also became part of its wider academic story. The donation linked Barkley’s interest in education with an achievement that had begun as two students working through a difficult mathematical problem.Barkley’s donation extended the impact of the students’ discoveryThe SportsRush reported that Barkley has previously made substantial donations to educational causes, including support for his alma mater, Auburn University. His $1 million pledge to St. Mary’s followed that broader pattern of giving, but this particular donation was directly connected to the achievement of Johnson and Jackson.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: El Nino, heat fuel destructive storms across Pacific
articles.summary: Environment News: A strengthening El Nino is stirring up a dangerous mix of typhoons and hurricanes across the Pacific, fuelling storms that have killed hundreds, disru.
articles.body: A strengthening El Nino is stirring up a dangerous mix of typhoons and hurricanes across the Pacific, fuelling storms that have killed hundreds, disrupted trade and caused billions of dollars in damage. Another storm neared Japan on Monday and more could be possible in the region through Nov.The situation stands in contrast to a very quiet Atlantic, which has had its calmest start since 1941. Pacific cyclones have caused more than 230 deaths since April, media reports show, while natural disasters - including three back-to-back storms - caused an estimated $8.5 billion in direct economic losses in China in July alone, according to US govt statistics.The disruption hasn't been confined to communities in the storms' paths. Container shipping giant Maersk issued an advisory this month saying a string of severe typhoons had caused congestion at some of the region's biggest ports, reducing on-time vessel arrivals.Driving the activity are two overlapping sources of ocean heat. El Nino, which occurs when the equatorial Pacific warms and the atmosphere above it reacts, has been strengthening since it emerged in June and is creating conditions that favour tropical cyclones across much of the Pacific. Twelve tropical cyclones formed across the basin and the South China Sea in Aug, the most in a single month since 1961, according to the Hong Kong Observatory.At the central and eastern Pacific, at least 17 systems have reached tropical storm strength, with six becoming hurricanes and four reaching major status with winds of 179 km per hour or more.This is a Bloomberg story.

articles.title: In 2019, a Florida resident spotted a car in a pond on Google Earth; police recovered the remains of a man missing for 22 years
articles.summary: US News: In 2019, a former resident of a Florida neighbourhood found what appeared to be a car in a pond during a Google search and alerted a current resident,.
articles.body: In 2019, a former resident of a Florida neighbourhood found what appeared to be a car in a pond during a Google search and alerted a current resident, who confirmed it with a drone and called police. Police recovered the remains of William Moldt, missing for 22 years. Moldt, who was 40 when he disappeared, had called his girlfriend at about 21:30 on the night he went missing and said he would be home soon. He left a club at around 23:00 and drove away alone. More than two decades later, a former resident spotted what appeared to be a car in the pond while viewing Google Earth imagery. A drone confirmed the vehicle, and police recovered Moldt’s remains from inside it.How Google Earth revealed William Moldt's sunken car in 2019Mr Moldt's sunken car was spotted by a previous resident of the area after "doing a Google search", police said. The man then contacted a current resident of Moon Bay Circle and told him what he had seen. The current resident used his personal drone to confirm that there was a car in the pond before contacting police.The BBC reported that a Charley Project report said the vehicle had been visible in a Google Earth satellite photograph of the area since 2007. The report said the vehicle had apparently not been noticed until 2019.How William Moldt disappeared after leaving a club in 1997On the night of his disappearance, Moldt left the club at about 23:00 local time, according to a report by the National Missing and Unidentified Persons System cited by the BBC. He left alone in his vehicle and did not appear intoxicated. The report described him as a quiet man who did not socialise much.The report also said Moldt was not a frequent drinker but had several drinks at the bar. At about 21:30, he had called his girlfriend and told her he would be home soon. He was never seen or heard from again. Police launched a missing-person investigation, but the case went cold.How police recovered William Moldt's car from a Florida pond in 2019On 28 August 2019, police were called to reports of a car in a pond in Moon Bay Circle, Wellington. The BBC reported that the vehicle was recovered from the water and skeletal remains were found inside. One week later, the remains were positively identified as belonging to Moldt.The Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office told the BBC that Moldt was presumed to have lost control of his vehicle and driven into the pond. However, the force said there had been “no evidence of that occurring” during the initial investigation into his disappearance.How a shift in water made William Moldt's sunken car visibleThe sheriff's office said that a shift in the water had made the car visible. Police spokeswoman Therese Barbera said: “You can't determine what happened that many years ago, what transpired.” She also said: “All we know is that he went missing off the face of the Earth, and now he's been discovered.”Barbera said it was a neighbour who reported the sunken car and that she was not aware of reports that Google Maps had been used. Moldt's family had been informed about the discovery of his remains.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Student representatives at IIT Bombay have issued an official statement following the death of student Sahil Wakode, saying they do not condone cheating or any form of academic misconduct, while calling for reforms to address systemic concerns within the institute.“We do not stand for or condone cheating or any form of academic misconduct. At the same time, the loss of our fellow student, Sahil, is a deeply tragic event that has compelled us to reflect on the systems and processes within our Institute,” the representatives said.They said the protest launched by students was not intended to justify academic misconduct, but was a collective effort to raise concerns over issues that had existed within the institute for some time and seek “meaningful and strong institutional reforms” to prevent similar circumstances in the future.The representatives also welcomed the open house held with the institute's Director and other members of the administration on Sunday, saying it gave students an opportunity to directly raise their concerns and questions.Back fair probe into Professor DoollaOn Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, the students clarified that they had never presumed his guilt or sought to prejudge the ongoing investigation.“We stand with Professor Doolla as a member of our faculty community and believe that the investigation must be allowed to proceed fairly and impartially,” they said.The students said their demand was for Doolla to be relieved of his administrative responsibilities as Dean of Administrative Affairs while the investigation is underway. They described this as a precautionary measure intended to ensure that the probe remains independent and cannot be influenced in any manner.“The findings and appropriate action should follow from the established investigative process,” the representatives said.Oppose external political influenceThe student representatives said concerns arising from Sahil’s death should remain student-led and be addressed within the institute.“The loss of Sahil should not become a platform for external political interests, organisations, or narratives to shape the concerns of the IIT Bombay student community,” they said.They added that the demands had emerged from students’ experiences and concerns on campus, and that the reform process should remain rooted in the student community and the institute.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Northeast US airports resume operations after telecom outage disrupts thousands of flights
articles.summary: US News: US airports across the Northeast began returning to normal on Monday after a telecommunications failure disrupted air traffic operations at several ma.
articles.body: US airports across the Northeast began returning to normal on Monday after a telecommunications failure disrupted air traffic operations at several major airports, causing more than 1,000 flight delays and cancellations.US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said the communications lines had been repaired and operations were gradually resuming, although passengers were still expected to face delays as airlines worked through the backlog."The telecom lines have been repaired, and all airport operations in the Northeast are resuming," Duffy said.What caused the disruptionThe disruption began at around 10 am after a circuit failure at the Federal Aviation Administration's Philadelphia Terminal Radar Approach Control facility knocked out radio and radar equipment used to manage aircraft around several airports.The failure affected New York's John F Kennedy International Airport, LaGuardia Airport and Newark Liberty International Airport, as well as Philadelphia, Teterboro and Westchester County airports.The outage meant that flights headed for some of the airports could not land and were instead held at their departure points or diverted to other airports.Flightradar24 said JFK and LaGuardia were added to the list of airports where departing flights were being held because of the FAA equipment failure. Newark, Teterboro, Philadelphia and Westchester County were also affected.Newark sees hundreds of diversionsNewark saw particularly heavy disruption. Flightradar24 said arrivals resumed at the airport later in the day after a prolonged halt."Arrivals have just resumed at Newark. No commercial flights landed at EWR between 09:38 and 17:22 local time today," Flightradar24 posted.By 5.30 pm local time, 107 flights had been diverted from Newark to 34 different airports, affecting 25 airlines, according to the flight-tracking service.Washington's Dulles International Airport received 19 of those diverted flights, while JFK took 12. United Airlines, which operates a major hub at Newark, was the airline most affected, with 70 diversions.A second failure made matters worseThe disruption was compounded when officials discovered that a newly installed fibre-optic backup system in New Jersey had also been damaged during construction work.Duffy said a fibre-optic line near an Amtrak railway line had been cut, affecting Verizon communication lines.FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the incident exposed weaknesses in the agency's existing infrastructure and called for changes to the network design."The network design is terrible. And if we don’t fix the network design, we’re going to continue having these failures," he said.The disruption came as New York prepared to host world leaders and ministers for the 81st United Nations General Assembly, adding to the importance of restoring normal airport operations.By around 6 pm, Duffy said the telecommunications lines had been repaired and airport operations across the Northeast were resuming. However, passengers were warned that delays could continue as airlines cleared the disruption's knock-on effects.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: James Monroe's 1,200-acre Virginia estate is finally becoming a state park after years of efforts to protect the former president's home
articles.summary: US News: For years, Oak Hill Farm sat in southern Loudoun County as a privately held piece of Virginia history, its fields and woodland surrounding the former .
articles.body: For years, Oak Hill Farm sat in southern Loudoun County as a privately held piece of Virginia history, its fields and woodland surrounding the former home of President James Monroe. The estate is now set for a different future. According to The Conservation Fund, in July 2026, Virginia lawmakers approved the acquisition of more than 1,200 acres at Oak Hill, clearing the way for the property to become the state's newest state park. The decision follows years of efforts by lawmakers, conservation groups and local residents to protect the land. It also places Monroe's former home within a larger public landscape that carries stories reaching beyond the fifth US president, including those of enslaved people and Indigenous communities connected to the area.Oak Hill preserves more than James Monroe's presidential historyOak Hill lies near Aldie, south of Leesburg, between James Monroe Highway, Little River Turnpike and Tail Race Road. The property contains farmland, forest and the house associated with Monroe, making it one of the remaining privately owned properties tied directly to a US founding-era president.Monroe lived at Oak Hill during the later part of his life. The estate is therefore connected to a period that followed his presidency, rather than simply serving as a site linked to his years in Washington.Its significance, however, is not limited to the person who owned it. The land also preserves evidence of the people who worked and lived there, including enslaved people, as well as the longer Indigenous history of the surrounding landscape.Virginia lawmakers push Oak Hill towards state park statusThe move towards state park status did not happen in a single legislative session. As reported by America’s State Parks, Del. John McAuliff, who represents parts of Fauquier and Loudoun counties, introduced House Bill 500 during Virginia's 2026 legislative session with the goal of securing the property for public ownership.Reportedly, the bill passed the House unanimously, 98-0. It was later carried forward into the 2027 legislative session, but the process changed when Gov. Abigail Spanberger included the Oak Hill acquisition in a budget amendment.The Virginia legislature voted to accept that amendment in July, completing the state's approval of the purchase.McAuliff had made preservation of Oak Hill one of his priorities during his first term. State Sen. Russet Perry, who represents parts of Loudoun and Fauquier counties, had also worked towards state park designation since taking office in 2024.Their efforts were part of a broader campaign involving local supporters and conservation organisations.A 1,200-acre estate was protected ahead of public ownershipThe Conservation Fund became a central part of the preservation effort before the state formally approved the park.Reportedly, the organisation purchased Oak Hill in November 2025, protecting the estate while arrangements for its eventual transfer to public ownership continued. That step kept the 1,200-plus acres together rather than allowing the historic property and surrounding land to face an uncertain future under private ownership.The fund's involvement also reflected the scale of the site. Oak Hill is not simply a historic house and a small surrounding garden. Its landscape stretches across farmland and forest, creating a substantial tract of open land in addition to the presidential connection.The eventual state park will therefore combine historic preservation with public access to a much larger landscape.More than 10,000 people joined the campaign for Oak HillThe campaign to preserve Oak Hill attracted support from well beyond the politicians directly involved. According to The Conservation Fund, more than 10,000 people supported the acquisition through petitions, letters and personal donations. That response helped demonstrate local and wider interest in keeping the property intact and securing public access.Heather Richards, the fund's Mid-Atlantic vice president, said the level of public involvement was unusually strong for one of the organisation's preservation projects.The campaign also brought together state officials, conservation advocates and members of the local community. The approval was presented by those involved as a bipartisan effort, with both Democratic legislators and the governor playing roles in moving the project forward.Oak Hill's history extends beyond James MonroeTurning Oak Hill into a state park will make the property accessible as public land, but its historical story extends well beyond Monroe's ownership.The estate's past includes the people who maintained the farm and household during an era when slavery was part of Virginia's social and economic system. The surrounding area also has Indigenous histories that predate Monroe and the establishment of the United States.Those layers are likely to shape how visitors understand the site. The house can tell the story of a former president, while the wider estate provides a setting for examining the people and communities whose lives were tied to the property.Oak Hill becomes Virginia's newest state parkThe acquisition adds more than 1,200 acres of farm and forest to Virginia's public estate and establishes Oak Hill as the state's newest state park. It also places Monroe's former home within a system designed to preserve historic and natural resources while allowing people to visit and use the land.The timing is closely tied to the 250th anniversary of American independence in 2026. State officials and supporters have pointed to the anniversary as an appropriate moment to secure the property for long-term public ownership.The transition does not erase the years of uncertainty that preceded it. Oak Hill reached state park status only after repeated legislative efforts, conservation work and a public campaign to keep the estate together.Now the property has a different status. What was once a privately held presidential estate is being preserved as public land, with its house, fields and forests set to remain part of Virginia's landscape for generations to come.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Thousands of US flights grounded for hours across major US airports, here's why
articles.summary: Tech News News: US travellers faced a tough situation when thousands of flights across United States were stopped on September 21 after a telecommunications outage. A.
articles.body: US travellers faced a tough situation when thousands of flights across United States were stopped on September 21 after a telecommunications outage. As reported by Reuters, the outage forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to halt arrivals at major East Coast airports. The report further reveals that the service disruption began around 9.45 am when constructions workers accidentally severed a telecom line in New Jersey which led to crippling of communications at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility. Many incoming flights were stopped at all the three major New York-area airports including JFK, LaGuardia, and Newark and Philadelphia, Boston, and two smaller New York-area airports due to the outage. The telecommunications outage lasted for around eight hours and led to widespread cancellation and flight diversions.Thousands of US flights grounded: What went wrongAs per the Reuters report, the trouble began around 9:45 a.m. when workers accidentally cut a telecom line the FAA relies on. The disruption forced the agency to halt incoming flights at all three major New York-area airports, along with Philadelphia, Boston, and two smaller New York-area airports. The problem wasn't fully resolved for roughly eight hours.According to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford, the outage traced back to a failed circuit at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility that handles traffic for the affected airports. When controllers tried switching to the backup system, they discovered the backup fiber line had also been damaged — a break Bedford said would take roughly 13 hours to fix on its own. A new circuit was being installed in the meantime to restore service faster.Government’s responseInitial blame shifted more than once through the day. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy first pointed to an Amtrak construction crew, saying it had accidentally cut into a fiber line near New Brunswick, New Jersey. Amtrak pushed back, denying responsibility. New Jersey Transit later said one of its own crews had been digging about 10 feet from utility markings at a nearby work site, and said it was still trying to determine whether Verizon or a contractor was responsible for those markings in the first place. Verizon confirmed it was working to repair the damaged cable and restore connectivity.Airports and flights affectedThe numbers were staggering. Flight-tracking site FlightAware reported around 7,000 flights delayed or canceled nationwide, including 1,400 flights at the three major New York-area airports alone. Newark Liberty International — a major hub for United Airlines — was hit hardest, with more than half of all flights there canceled; United issued a travel waiver to help affected passengers. More than 100 flights were diverted to other airports altogether.Reagan Washington National Airport also briefly paused flights for over an hour due to volume issues, and Philadelphia saw a second ground stop before flights resumed later in the afternoon. Boston's ground stop, triggered by spillover traffic from the other closures, was eventually lifted as well.Services restoredBy around 5:30 p.m., New Jersey Transit said most of the fiber cables had been repaired and were coming back online.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Watch: Press pool boycott leaves Trump barely audible at White House event
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump was barely audible during live coverage of a White House event on Monday after major television networks suspended pooled co.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump was barely audible during live coverage of a White House event on Monday after major television networks suspended pooled coverage following his decision to bar CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.During the event, Trump unveiled a new helipad on the White House South Lawn and spoke with construction workers. However, the sound of Marine One drowned out much of his speech with TV pool cameras and microphones absent.In a video shared bu Clash Report, Trump was seen cutting a ribbon on the walkway leading to the new helipad and interacting with workers. His comments, however, were inaudible on the White House livestream.Meanwhile, the White House subsequently launched 'Trump TV', a 24/7 streaming platform featuring administration announcements, presidential remarks and coverage related to the US President.The five networks that make up the White House TV pool - ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC - suspended pooled coverage after Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House grounds, citing “fake news”.“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organisation because it objects to its reporting,” the five networks said in a joint statement.The White House press pool is a rotating group of journalists who travel with the president and share reporting, audio and video with other news organisations. With the TV pool absent, there was no standard pool microphone or live feed to clearly capture Trump’s remarks during the helipad event.C-SPAN also said it would not air the ceremony because it relies on the TV pool and did not have a feed.The White House later launched “Trump TV”, a 24/7 streaming platform featuring administration announcements, presidential remarks and other coverage related to Trump.The episode highlighted the immediate impact of the White House’s press restrictions, with little independent broadcast footage available from the helipad event in the absence of the TV pool.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Google has finally started taking pre-orders for its all new Googlebook laptops. Launched in May this year, the laptop mark Google’s most ambitious push into AI-driven personal computing, positioning Googlebook as a premium alternative to traditional Chromebooks. Shipping begins October 4 in the US and October 5 in Canada, the UK, Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia. The tech giant says that GoogleBook is designed to be a laptop with AI at its core by combining the speed of the Chrome browser, the vast library of Google Play apps and a modern design built specifically for the new Gemini Intelligence platform.Google CEO Sundar Pichai also took to social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) to post by the Googlebook. Pichai shared a video of the Googlebook laptop along with a caption which reads, ‘Feeling good about this one:)’.Googlebook pre-order details⁃Price: Starting at $899. every Googlebook includes 12 months of Google AI Pro providing 5TB of cloud storage and our Gemini Advanced tools, plus 3 months of YouTube Premium, Adobe Photoshop, and more. Googlebook OS also comes with regular feature drops and updates for up to 10 years.⁃Availability: Pre-orders are now open on the Google Store, Best Buy, and other select retailers. Devices arrive on shelves starting October 4 in the U.S., and October 5 in Canada, the U.K., Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia.⁃Partners: Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo are producing the first models.Googlebook featuresFirst unveiled in May, Googlebook is designed to offer a genuine step up from traditional Chromebooks rather than replacing them. Initial models come from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, running on either Intel Core Ultra or Qualcomm Snapdragon X Elite processors, with up to 14 hours of battery life. Devices start with 16GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, weigh under 2.85 pounds, and are built with premium materials including aluminium, magnesium, and carbon fiber. Displays are 2.8K OLED touchscreens, and the laptops include biometric authentication via face or fingerprint unlock, along with a dedicated "G" key for one-touch searches.Under the hood, Googlebook runs on Android OS paired with a desktop version of the Chrome browser and familiar ChromeOS elements, blending Google's two operating system foundations into one device — the company's most ambitious push for a flagship ChromeOS showcase since the Pixelbook in 2017 and Pixelbook Go in 2019.Gemini AI integration•Magic Pointer: Contextual AI suggestions when hovering over content (translations, calendar prompts, price comparisons).•Continue On: Resume tasks started on Android phones directly from the Googlebook taskbar.•Omni AI Features: Drafting text, organizing information, creating widgets, and real-time content understanding.•On-Device AI: Dedicated NPUs delivering 45+ TOPS for local AI workloads, reducing reliance on cloud processingGet the latest technology news and updates.
